subject.title: Slack button interactions should dispatch a reply turn, not a heartbeat wake (follow-up to #99544)

question: Should Slack reply button/select clicks remain heartbeat-owned system events, or should Slack synthesize normal inbound reply turns for user-initiated controls?
rationale: The source-proven gap is real, but changing it replaces a recently merged Slack interaction design and crosses Slack plugin, channel reply dispatch, system-event draining, and session-conflict behavior.

options.title: Move Reply Controls To Inbound Turns
options.body: Treat user-initiated Slack reply controls like normal channel input, with tests and live proof for clicked value, thread delivery, and busy-run behavior.

options.title: Keep Heartbeat And Harden It
options.body: Retain the system-event heartbeat design, but require proof that values, visible replies, and retry behavior are reliable end to end.

options.title: Wait For Shared Conflict Review
options.body: Defer the owner choice until the broader reply-session init conflict work is reviewed, then retest Slack interactions against that recovery layer.

recommendation.title: Move Reply Controls To Inbound Turns
recommendation.body: Treat user-initiated Slack reply controls like normal channel input, with tests and live proof for clicked value, thread delivery, and busy-run behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision crosses the core reply assembly path and the Slack interaction channel-runtime boundary where steipete has recent architecture history.
